angle_name: Canonical-shell signed dispersion via the δ-method and Kuznetsov
mechanism: Put X=(Y+1)^2-1 and H=Y. Replace each prime-counting error by the centered prime measure ν(n)=1_{n prime}-∫_n^{n+1}du/log u, absorbing the harmless discretization separately, and set a_Y(m)=Σ_{d≤Y, d|m} μ(d)ν(m/d). Then S(Y,X-t) is the endpoint sum Σ_{m≤X-t}a_Y(m) up to O(X^{1/2+o(1)}) smooth terms. Expand the H-point second moment before taking absolute values. A smooth dyadic partition and the δ-method turn its off-diagonal part into signed shifted-convolution forms dp-eq=h weighted by μ(d)μ(e)ν(p)ν(q) and by the exact endpoint Gram kernel. Apply exact Heath-Brown identities to ν(p),ν(q), retaining μ(d)μ(e), then Kuznetsov plus a spectral large sieve to sum simultaneously over h,d,e and the δ-moduli. The decisive range is d,e,p,q≈Y; unbalanced ranges should succumb to ordinary bilinear large-sieve estimates. At the canonical shell, Y^2<n<(Y+1)^2, any representation n=dp with d≤Y and p prime has p>Y and is unique, so the moving-boundary contribution has no divisor-fiber multiplicity. The constant/Cesàro mode must be included in the same signed dispersion calculation, not estimated separately.
new_leverage: The new leverage is the conjunction of the sanctioned canonical window and the square-shell uniqueness p>Y: the boundary portion of the Gram form becomes a genuine one-large-prime bilinear sequence rather than the Wigert-sized divisor sum seen at arbitrary points. Spectral summation then treats the growing pair-to-modulus fibers in L2 instead of requiring a bounded-fiber map. This passes walls 2, 3, and 8 while preserving the μ×prime sign interaction required by wall 1. It does not claim that uniqueness alone controls the accumulated zero mode; that mode is explicitly part of the proposed signed Kuznetsov estimate.
target_estimate: Canonical signed spectral-dispersion estimate: for X=(Y+1)^2-1, H=Y, and the exact endpoint weight Ω_H(m,n;X)=#{0≤t<H:max(m,n)≤X-t}, prove Σ_{d,e≤Y} μ(d)μ(e) Σ_{p,q} ν(p)ν(q) Ω_H(dp,eq;X) ≪_ε H X^{1+ε}. After the stated discretization this is exactly Σ_{t<H}|S(Y,X-t)|^2≪_ε H X^{1+ε}. The analytic core is the corresponding bound for every balanced dyadic block d,e,p,q≈Y after δ-symbol expansion, uniformly in the endpoint/Cesàro frequency.

obstacle_positions.1: The μ(d)μ(e) weights remain inside the prime-prime shifted convolution through Kuznetsov; no Mertens-energy input or Cauchy recombination over d is used.
obstacle_positions.2: No pair→modulus map is asserted: all growing fibers and conductors up to O(Y^2)=O(X) are summed spectrally with their natural L2 multiplicity.
obstacle_positions.3: The estimate is formulated on the exact backward window at X=(Y+1)^2-1, so the proved excursion transfer applies directly.
obstacle_positions.4: Only δ/Kuznetsov conductors arising from d,e and shifts, at most polynomial in X, occur; the enormous wheel modulus never appears.
obstacle_positions.5: This is not an upper-bound sieve: exact prime identities are followed by signed Type-II and spectral cancellation with the linear Möbius weights intact.
obstacle_positions.6: No zero enumeration or pointwise bound for R is used; a fixed saving would come from finite shifted-convolution cancellation and therefore does not assume a zero-free strip.
obstacle_positions.7: Numerics play no evidentiary role; they would be used only to check normalizations and detect missing diagonal terms.
obstacle_positions.8: No L∞ control of unit increments is required. Moreover, inside the canonical square shell the prime part of an increment has at most one representation d·p, while the full argument uses the amortized Gram kernel.
obstacle_positions.9: There is no renewal or smaller-scale absolute-value induction. Heath-Brown identities are used with their honest supports solely to create signed Type-II forms.

kill_test: For one smooth balanced block d,e,p,q∈[Y/2,2Y], derive the δ-symbol/Kuznetsov formula including the endpoint zero mode and compare the spectral large-sieve loss with the diagonal size. Kill the angle immediately if the best available bound is ≥H X^2, or if isolating the zero mode forces |μ| or |ν| before spectral summation. A computational algebra check at small Y can verify the exact Ω_H expansion and square-shell uniqueness but cannot validate the estimate.
rung1_version: Prove the same canonical dispersion bound with H X^{2-2δ+ε} for some fixed δ>0. It suffices to obtain any uniform power saving in the balanced dyadic block while treating all unbalanced blocks and smooth/discretization errors at that scale. The excursion theorem then yields S(Y,X)≪X^{1-δ+ε}.
plausible_partial: Give an exact, Lean-formalizable reduction of the canonical windowed second moment to the Ω_H-weighted four-variable form; prove the square-shell uniqueness lemma; separate the diagonal, smooth Li discretization, prime-power terms introduced by exact identities, and all dyadic ranges; then dispose of the ranges with min(d,e)≤Y^{1-η} or strongly unbalanced Heath-Brown factors by existing large-sieve bounds. The bounded-effort deliverable is a theorem reducing both rung 1 and rung 2 to one explicitly stated balanced signed Kuznetsov block, with no hidden absolute-value loss.
weakest_assumption: A hybrid Kuznetsov large-sieve estimate giving a fixed power saving for the balanced μ(d)μ(e)-weighted prime-prime shifted convolution, uniformly over the δ-moduli, shifts, and the endpoint Cesàro mode. For rung 2 the same estimate must reach square-root scale; for rung 1 any fixed saving suffices.
